chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from al-Washa, from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'This pigeon — the pigeon of the Sanctuary — it is from the lineage of the pigeon of Ismail ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon him) which belonged to him.'

key_terms.إسماعيل بن إبراهيم: Ismail son of Ibrahim — the prophet Ishmael, who with his father Ibrahim built the Ka'ba
key_terms.الحرم: The Sanctuary/Haram — the sacred precinct of Mecca surrounding the Ka'ba
key_terms.الحمام: Pigeon/dove — specifically the pigeons that inhabit the Sacred Sanctuary in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the pigeons in the Haram of Mecca according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identified the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram of Mecca) as being descended from the personal pigeons of Prophet Ismail ibn Ibrahim (peace be upon both of them). This hadith connects the sacred birds of the Haram to the Abrahamic heritage of the holy sanctuary itself, indicating a deep continuity between the prophetic household and the sanctity of the Haram. The original audience of Abu Khadija, a close companion of the Imam, would have understood this as affirming the blessed status of those doves and possibly as a basis for their protection.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Al Washa, from Ahmad Bin A’aiz, from Abu Khadeeja who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘This pigeon here, pigeon of the Sanctuary, it is from the lineage of a pigeon of Ismail<sup>as</sup> Bin Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> which was for him<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from al-Washsha’ from Ahmad ibn ‘A’idh from abu Khadijah who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘These pigeons -the pigeons of al-Haram (the sacred area) - are of the offspring of the pigeon of Tsma‘il ibn Ibrahim, ‘Alayhima al-Salam, that belonged to him.’”
